title: Add crash recovery, workspace snapshots, and migration evidence
summary: Board and Studio workspace editing can recover from crashes, interrupted saves, corrupt assets, schema changes, stale imported truth, and failed proposal generation without silently losing or overwriting user work.
acceptance_criteria: A repository-owned versioned stewardship contract defines the exact domain records, source of truth, ownership boundary, compatibility policy, and unsupported capabilities for this slice.
Every exported record uses repository-qualified identity, producer revision, explicit timestamps, deterministic canonical serialization, content integrity, and correction/supersession links.

Fields are classified by visibility and sensitivity; secrets, credentials, personal paths, full URLs, precise locations, private media names, health/family/customer narrative, and unrelated payloads are excluded or conservatively redacted by default.

Lifecycle states distinguish active, stale, unavailable, partial, corrected, superseded, revoked, expired, inaccessible, corrupt, unsupported-version, and deleted/tombstoned posture without mapping missing data to success.
Retention, export, backup, restore, correction, deletion, revocation, and derived-data invalidation are explicit and domain-specific; unsupported operations are declared rather than implied.

A generated quality/support evidence snapshot identifies what was checked, with which rule/tool version, against which source revision and environment, what was omitted, and when the evidence expires.
Generation and retry are deterministic and idempotent for unchanged source state; repeated execution cannot duplicate domain actions or silently rewrite earlier receipts.
Migration preserves historical identity and evidence, handles newer or unknown schema conservatively, and creates a safety copy or forward-only warning before irreversible transformation.
Offline and local operation remain useful; HumbleControl and cross-app consumers are optional readers and never become a runtime dependency for the domain feature.
No restore, deletion, correction, upload, support handoff, or external mutation occurs without a human-readable preview and validation by the repository/domain owner.
Fixtures cover normal, empty, stale, unavailable dependency, partial data, duplicate, corrupt, unsupported version, redacted, correction, deletion/revocation, interruption, and recovery.
The producer can conform to Quality Evidence, Data Lifecycle, Support Bundle, Artifact Envelope, registry, and intent/receipt protocols while remaining independently testable.
Recovery uses atomic primary saves, journals or checkpoints, bounded versioned snapshots, asset integrity, and explicit clean/dirty/recovered/conflicted document state.
Opening after interruption previews recovered commands, missing assets, stale source references, migration changes, and the exact base revision before applying recovery.
Migration and recovery produce durable evidence with source/target schema, command IDs, rejected operations, safety copy, and user decision.
The strongest repository-native tests, builds, static checks, migration/fixture checks, contract validation, and diff hygiene pass with zero app-owned warnings.

agent_notes: Portfolio Stewardship Wave 4; repository-owned technical stewardship contract.
Estimated effort: L, approximately 8-20 focused working hours after prerequisites; split only when evidence proves a stable smaller boundary.
Implementation risk: medium-high because lifecycle, privacy, recovery, support, release, or learning semantics can affect durable user trust.
Cross-repository platform prerequisites: mrPoky/HumbleControl#HC-0167, mrPoky/HumbleControl#HC-0168, mrPoky/HumbleControl#HC-0171.
Non-scope: Do not implement cloud sync or multiplayer, retain unbounded full-document history, silently apply recovered AI changes, or overwrite newer imported source truth.
Alternative considered and rejected: Autosave one latest JSON file — a single mutable snapshot cannot distinguish clean save, partial write, stale source, migration, or recoverable command history.
Do not weaken the application, fabricate evidence, convert unavailable data to success, hide warnings, broaden consent, or centralize domain ownership to satisfy this ticket.
Close only after repository-native tests/builds, fixture and migration evidence, accessibility/privacy review where applicable, and zero app-owned warnings.
Wave 8 portfolio reassessment: retain; priority band next. Data lifecycle, recovery, supportability, and transparent learning are professional product requirements.
Wave 10 final rationalization: retain-operational; portfolio band later. Lifecycle, recovery, support, and transparent feedback remain professional operations work.
Wave 11 execution reconciliation: `supporting-input`. Use the Wave 11 implementation program as the delivery entry point while preserving this ticket's evidence and intent.

Wave 12 deep reassessment: decision `retain-supporting`, relevance `next`, current priority `medium`, execution gate `sequence behind current correctness and the bounded delivery program`. Lifecycle, privacy, recovery, support, and transparent learning remain professional requirements.
Wave 13 human-validation reassessment: `retain-operational-input` / `next` / priority `medium`. Lifecycle, privacy, recovery, support, and feedback are required for trustworthy beta use.

Final Wave 14 validity review: `valid`; publication `publish-after-fresh-reconciliation`; implementation sequence `after-sudoku`. Lifecycle, privacy, recovery, support, and feedback are required for trustworthy beta use.
